4:1.sourceText: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν εὑρηκέναι Ἀβραὰμ τὸν προπάτορα ἡμῶν κατὰ σάρκα;
4:1.targetText: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather, has discovered?

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
This BSB wording leaves κατὰ σάρκα ("according to the flesh") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces the reported statement; the Greek uses an infinitive.

4:2.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ Ἀβραὰμ ἐξ ἔργων ἐδικαιώθη, ἔχει καύχημα· ἀλλ’ οὐ πρὸς Θεόν,
4:2.targetText: If Abraham was indeed justified by works, he had something to boast about, but not before God.

groups.note: γάρ ("for") is rendered indeed.
καύχημα ("a boast") is rendered something to boast about.

4:3.sourceText: τί γὰρ ἡ γραφὴ λέγει; Ἐπίστευσεν δὲ Ἀβραὰμ τῷ Θεῷ, καὶ ἐλογίσθη αὐτῷ εἰς δικαιοσύνην.
4:3.targetText: For what does the Scripture say? “Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ in the quotation untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:4.sourceText: τῷ δὲ ἐργαζομένῳ ὁ μισθὸς οὐ λογίζεται κατὰ χάριν ἀλλὰ κατὰ ὀφείλημα·
4:4.targetText: Now the wages of the worker are not credited as a gift, but as an obligation.

groups.note: The dative τῷ ἐργαζομένῳ ("to the one who works") is rendered of the worker.
κατά ("according to") is rendered as.
χάριν ("grace, favor") is rendered a gift.

4:5.sourceText: τῷ δὲ μὴ ἐργαζομένῳ, πιστεύοντι δὲ ἐπὶ τὸν δικαιοῦντα τὸν ἀσεβῆ, λογίζεται ἡ πίστις αὐτοῦ εἰς δικαιοσύνην,
4:5.targetText: However, to the one who does not work, but believes in Him who justifies the wicked, his faith is credited as righteousness.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:6.sourceText: καθάπερ καὶ Δαυεὶδ λέγει τὸν μακαρισμὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ᾧ ὁ Θεὸς λογίζεται δικαιοσύνην χωρὶς ἔργων

groups.note: καθάπερ ("just as") is rendered likewise.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:7.sourceText: Μακάριοι ὧν ἀφέθησαν αἱ ἀνομίαι καὶ ὧν ἐπεκαλύφθησαν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι·
4:7.targetText: “Blessed are they whose lawless acts are forgiven, whose sins are covered.

groups.note: The relative ὧν ("of whom") is rendered they whose.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB joins the two clauses with a comma; καί has no English word.

ἀκροβυστίαν ("uncircumcision") is rendered the uncircumcised.
